prompt:
I need the front end for Benchtop Family Notebook. A shared lab notebook for families doing science-fair and backyard experiments together, where kids, parents and relatives in other homes can log data and leave feedback without overwriting the kid's own work.

Who's using it: Marcus Oyelaran, a father helping his 12-year-old daughter Temi with her seventh-grade science-fair project on whether mealworms can eat polystyrene foam. He's an accountant, not a scientist, and checks the notebook after work.

What they're doing right now: Overnight, two things changed. Temi rewrote her hypothesis, and Grandma Funmi, who is running a duplicate set of containers at her house two hours away, added her week-3 weigh-ins. Marcus notices that one of Grandma's containers shows foam mass going up, which looks like a data-entry slip. The fair rules say the student must write the hypothesis and conclusions herself. So he wants to see exactly what each person changed since Sunday, leave a question for Grandma on the suspect reading, and comment on Temi's new hypothesis without editing it.

What's in the system at this point: There are 4 containers at home (foam only, oats only, foam+oats, and a no-food control) and 2 at Grandma's (foam only, foam+oats), each starting with 50 mealworms. There are 21 days of weigh-ins: foam mass in grams to 0.01 g, worm count, and number of dead worms. There are 18 photos. Roles: Temi owns the hypothesis, procedure and conclusion sections; Marcus and Grandma Funmi can add data and comments only; Temi's science teacher, Ms. Albrecht, has read-only access. The change history since Sunday has 9 edits, including Temi's hypothesis rewrite (Mon 9:14pm) and Grandma's 4 new readings (Tue 7:02am). Grandma's foam+oats container shows 3.12 g on day 14 and 3.41 g on day 21. The fair deadline is Dec 5.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
